get.data: { domain_key, entity, entity_id, id, name, slug }[]

Actor.description:
The IAM-resolved caller. On `/v1/me` the profile fields and `permissions` are
fetched from IAM per request; in local-auth mode only `id` is populated.

permissions.description:
The decision for each permission key checked on this request. A key absent
from the map is denied.

creator_actor_id.description:
Attribution, not ownership: there is deliberately no foreign key to any
user table and no cascade, so a board survives its creator being removed
from IAM and stays attributed to them.

creator_name.description:
Denormalised at creation so attribution survives the actor's removal from
IAM.

composition_elements.description:
Controls and layout containers — date pickers, dropdowns, section headers.
They draw from no Dataset, which is what distinguishes them from Widgets,
and Analytics stores their configuration verbatim for the composition
surface.

DashboardScopeLevel.description:
The access floor of a published Dashboard, from most restrictive to most open:

- `personal` — the creator only
- `department` — the department named in `scope_organizational_ref`
- `role` — the role named in `scope_organizational_ref`
- `organization` — every authenticated user

The scope is a floor, not a whitelist: a Share Grant refines access within it
and can never elevate anyone above it.

is_pinned.description: Whether the calling viewer pinned it.

DataClassification.description:
The sensitivity tag: an ordered ladder, least sensitive first.

| Value | Means |
|---|---|
| `public` | May be seen by anyone who can reach the portal. |
| `internal` | Ordinary company data. The default. |
| `confidential` | Restricted to those with a reason — money movement, customer records, anything commercially sensitive. |
| `restricted` | The narrowest tier: material that would cause serious harm if disclosed. |

It answers **how protected** the data is, which is a different question from
**is it about an identifiable person** — that one is answered by
`exposes_personal_data`, so a Dataset can be `confidential` *and* personal.

On amendment a classification may be **raised but never lowered**, at any step
of the ladder: the data already went out under the higher label.

DataShape.description:
The structural properties that decide which Visualization Families may present
a Dataset.

has_coordinate_pair.description: Both a latitude and a longitude.

has_many_records.description:
From the Dataset's `record_volume`: thousands or millions of rows. A
histogram over one pre-aggregated figure is not a histogram.

Dataset.description:
A Dataset declaration. Metadata only — it points at data the Source System
serves and holds none of it.

accountable_department_id.description: The IAM department accountable for the data.

created_by_actor_id.description:
The IAM actor who published this Dataset. Attribution only — no foreign
key, so the row survives its author being removed from IAM.

exposes_personal_data.description:
Whether this Dataset exposes personal data. Stated explicitly and kept
separate from `classification` because it drives an access-recording
obligation and must not be inferred.

grain.description:
The row grain: the Field keys whose combination identifies one row, or an
empty list where the endpoint answers with a single summary row. Lets an
Author tell a one-row summary from thousands of records.

iam_product_id.description:
The publishing product, as IAM defines it. Never reassignable: the
permission key and the endpoint both belong to it.

id.description: Dotted lowercase segments. Appears in URLs and Widget bindings.

path.description:
Absolute path appended to the Source System's registered base URL. No
query string, fragment, or traversal.

required_permission_key.description:
The IAM key that gates this Dataset's **data**, checked against the viewer
at query time. Normally the owning product's own read permission, not an
Analytics key — that indirection is what stops a Widget becoming an IAM
bypass. Immutable once published.

source_system_id.description:
The registered deployment whose base URL the path resolves against. Must
belong to `iam_product_id` — publishing against another product's
deployment is refused.

time_dimension_field.description:
Names a declared date Dimension, or is omitted. Trend and temporal
Visualization Families need it, and it may not move once published.

updated_by_actor_id.description:
The actor who last amended it. Tracked separately because an amendment
changes what every bound Widget sees, long after publication.

Envelope.description: The shape of every response, success or failure.

aggregations.description:
Measures only, and at least one is required. Each must be meaningful for
the Field type — a user identifier supports `count` and `distinct-count`
but never `sum`, which is what makes that declaration impossible.

filter_operators.description: How the Field may be filtered when filterable. Must suit the Field type.

filterable.description:
Must be stated explicitly — an omitted value is an undeclared Field, not a
default.

key.description: Stable unique identifier; must match the key the Source System returns.

orderable.description: Must be stated explicitly, as with filterable.

FieldRole.description:
A `dimension` is groupable and filterable (country, status); a `measure` is
aggregatable (amount, count). Every Field is exactly one of the two.

FieldSemantic.description:
What a Field *means*, where its `type` and `role` cannot say.

A type says how a value is stored and a role says whether it groups or
aggregates. Neither can say that a number is a latitude, that a category holds
a workflow state, or that a sum is meaningful — `aggregations: [sum]` permits
the arithmetic, it does not claim the total means anything, and summing
percentages is permitted and meaningless.

| Value | Marks | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| `geographic-area` | a named place — country, region, administrative area | the choropleth in Geospatial |
| `geographic-latitude` / `geographic-longitude` | a coordinate pair; **both** are needed, one alone plots nothing | the point map in Geospatial |
| `state` | a condition at a point in time — settled, pending, failed | Status |
| `stage` | an ordered step in a process; the order is what a funnel reads | the flow half of Ranking & Flow |
| `additive-total` | a Measure whose sum means something | Composition |

**Optional.** A Dataset without semantics is still publishable — it simply is
not offered the Families that turn on meaning. `additive-total`,
`geographic-latitude` and `geographic-longitude` are declared on Measures; the
rest on Dimensions, and a mismatch is refused at publication.

FilterParameter.description:
A parameter callers may pass through to the Source System. Publishing one is a
promise to callers: it may not later vanish.

allowed_values.description: When present, a value outside this list is refused.

name.description: The query parameter name sent upstream.

required.description: The endpoint cannot answer without it.

PresentationOption.description: One Visualization Family the Data Shape satisfies.

requirement.example: at least one Measure and a Time Dimension

single_value.description:
True for families whose widgets render one aggregated figure (stat card,
delta, status badge). When true, back the Widget with an aggregate-shaped
Dataset — the Source System returns the figure over the received filters;
Analytics and the frontend never compute it.

visualization_types.description: The concrete Visualization Types in this Family.

ReadinessChecks.description:
Only `database` gates readiness. Optional dependencies are reported so an
operator can see them, but never make the service unready.

RecordVolume.description:
Roughly how many rows this Dataset answers with. Optional.

It exists for the one question a Field-level `semantic` cannot answer, because
it belongs to the Dataset: **is this many records?** A histogram over one
pre-aggregated figure is not a histogram, and nothing else settles it — a grain
of `["day", "corridor"]` may be forty rows or four million, depending on
cardinalities nobody declares.

An order of magnitude on purpose. It decides whether a distribution is worth
offering, not what one draws, and a publisher made to keep a count accurate
would stop keeping it at all.

`single-row` must agree with an empty `grain`; a contradiction is refused.
Only **Distribution** reads it, and only `thousands` and `millions` satisfy it.

ShareCandidate.description:
Someone a Dashboard may be shared with. `target_type` and `target_ref` are
exactly what a Share Grant needs, so the client passes them straight through.

base_url.description: The origin this deployment's Dataset paths resolve against.

created_by_actor_id.description:
The IAM actor who created this. Attribution only — no foreign key, so the
row survives its author being removed from IAM.

updated_by_actor_id.description: The actor who last changed it.

base_url.description:
Absolute `http`/`https` origin with a host and no query string or
fragment — a query string here would inject parameters into every Dataset
the product serves. A trailing slash is trimmed. A bare host without the
scheme is refused.

iam_product_id.description:
The product's own `id` from `/v1/source-systems/iam-products` — a UUID.
Neither its `slug` (the readable name) nor its `entity_id` (the owning
entity) is accepted; sending the slug is refused with the id to use.

id.description:
Stable slug for this deployment, used in Dataset declarations. Lowercase,
hyphen or underscore separated.

name.description: Defaults to the product's name in IAM.

TimeRange.description:
The two Filter Parameters that are the ends of a date range, and the Field they
narrow. Optional — and its **absence is a statement**: this endpoint takes no
range, rather than one whose parameter names a client should guess.

Guessing is the alternative this exists to remove. A parameter named `start`
that means something else accepts a date without complaint and returns the
wrong rows, under a chart nobody has reason to doubt.

Every name is checked at publication: `field` must be a declared Field, and
both parameters declared Filter Parameters.

TokenBundle.description: An IAM access token plus its refresh token.

field.description: The offending field, using dotted and indexed paths.

message.example: "money" is not a known Field type

Widget.description:
One data-bound visual instance. A Widget draws from exactly one Dataset and
cannot span Datasets. Composition Elements — controls and layout containers —
are not Widgets and carry no Dataset binding.

default_filters.description:
Filter values applied unless a viewer changes an exposed one. Keys must be
published Filter Parameters of the bound Dataset.

exposed_filters.description:
Which published Filter Parameters the viewer may change. Every entry must
be declared by the Dataset, otherwise the viewer is offered a control that
cannot work.

presentation_options.description:
Rendering settings, opaque to Analytics. The composition surface owns their
meaning; every option has a default, so an absent value is never an error.

visualization_type.description:
Must belong to a Family the bound Dataset's Data Shape satisfies — checked
on save, so a stored Widget can never reference a chart its Dataset could
not render.

WidgetLayout.description: Grid position and size, as sent by the composition surface.

bearerAuth.description:
An IAM access token. Verified in-process against IAM's pinned RS256 public
key; `token_use` must be `access`.
